plan.name: Third Shot Drops & Drives
plan.notes: Partner splits time 50/50 by rotating roles within each block, not by alternating blocks.

scoring.description: Record makes out of 10 for every block with a goal value. Blocks with goal null are unscored.

blocks.name: Warmup
blocks.description: Crosscourt and straight dinks, then five minutes of mid-court resets. Partner feeds medium pace at your feet from the kitchen; you absorb into the NVZ.

blocks.name: Stationary drops
blocks.description: Partner feeds a consistent ball from the kitchen; you drop crosscourt from the baseline. Switch every 20 balls.
blocks.coaching_point: Target is the kitchen, but apex is the real measure — the ball should peak on your side of the net.

blocks.name: Drop off a real return
blocks.description: Serve for real. Partner returns deep, you drop the third.
blocks.coaching_point: A deep return is what breaks this shot in a game. Returns must push you behind the baseline.

blocks.name: Drop and advance
blocks.description: Same as the previous block, then move in, reset whatever comes back, and play out the point.
blocks.coaching_point: The drop is the first shot of a transition, not a standalone skill.

blocks.name: Pressure games
blocks.description: Third-shot-only games to 7. Serving team starts at the baseline, receiving team at the kitchen.

sessions.label: Session B — Drives and shot selection

blocks.name: Drive mechanics
blocks.description: Partner feeds from the kitchen; you drive at their hip or paddle-side shoulder. Low to high, contact out in front, clearing the net by two feet or less.
blocks.coaching_point: A drive is a setup, not a winner.

blocks.name: Drive then fifth-shot drop
blocks.description: You drive the third, partner blocks it back, you drop the fifth and move in.
blocks.coaching_point: Highest-value block in the week. Most players drive well, then never recover the kitchen.

blocks.name: Read and choose
blocks.description: Partner varies return depth randomly. Deep means drop, short or medium means drive. Call the shot out loud the instant you read the bounce.
blocks.coaching_point: Scores decisions, not execution. A correct call executed poorly still counts as correct.

blocks.name: Live points
blocks.description: Full points to 11, no restrictions, starting from the serve.

progression.description: Consistent feeds, predictable returns, generous targets. Anywhere in the kitchen counts as a made drop.
Shrink the targets and add variation. Partner occasionally poaches in the later blocks so you hit to a place rather than at a person.

regression_rule.action: Return to the easier target for one session. Grinding at a target you cannot hit teaches the miss.

exit_criteria: Hitting week 3-4 targets consistently: drops 7/10 to the front half of the kitchen, correct calls 8/10
Third shot is no longer the shot losing points in live play
No movement in the log across three consecutive sessions (change the drill, get video, or get a lesson)

supporting_habits.description: Film one rep set from the sideline — Session A block 2 or Session B block 2. Most drop faults are a late paddle face or contact behind the hip, neither of which you can feel while hitting.
Play live games between drill sessions. Drilling without live play builds a shot that works against a cooperative feed.

drop: Contact behind the hip, forcing a wrist lift instead of a shoulder lift
Wrist flicking at the ball rather than a quiet paddle and lifting arm
Stopping in no-man's land instead of continuing to the kitchen line
Aiming at the net tape rather than the apex on your own side
drive: Swinging for a winner instead of a setup
Driving only at the paddle-side elbow; mix in hip and feet
Driving a ball that has dropped below net height
Admiring it instead of splitting to the transition zone for the fifth

fields.name: notes
fields.hint: What changed, not how it felt. e.g. 'partner started hitting returns deeper'
